statements.statement: The longer leg of an LED is the cathode (negative side).
statements.explanation: The longer leg is the anode (positive side). The shorter leg is the cathode (negative side).

statements.statement: If you connect an LED backwards, it will be damaged permanently.
statements.explanation: Connecting an LED backwards simply means it won't light up. No harm is done -- just flip it around to fix it.

statements.statement: The flat edge on an LED's plastic casing marks the cathode (negative side).
statements.explanation: The flat edge on the LED casing is a visual indicator for the cathode, which is helpful when the legs have been trimmed to equal length.

statements.statement: LEDs work regardless of which direction they are connected.
statements.explanation: LEDs only work when connected the correct way around, with the anode to positive and cathode to negative. They are directional like all diodes.
